titulo: Your weather app says it feels like nineteen below. Your car doesn't feel that.
receta: regla con numero + debate de una palabra (real o feels-like)
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que sabe de clima a su amigo que dice que el auto o las canerias estan a 'diez bajo cero' por la sensacion termica
regla_guardable: Wind chill is for people and animals. Pipes and cars only get as cold as the real air temperature.

interaccion.guardar: Wind chill = people and pets. Pipes and cars never go below the real air temperature. 0°F + 15 mph wind = -19°F wind chill; exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes.
interaccion.comentar: Which do you check: the real temperature or the feels-like?

fuentes: National Weather Service, Wind Chill Chart and Wind Chill Safety (weather.gov/safety/cold-wind-chill-chart): wind chill is how cold people and animals feel; it is based on heat loss from exposed skin; it does not make objects colder than the air temperature, only cools them faster; 0°F with 15 mph wind = -19°F wind chill; at -19°F wind chill exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes; frostbite requires actual air temperature below freezing

frases.texto: The National Weather Service says wind chill is how cold it feels to people and animals.
Wind cools objects faster, but never below the actual air temperature.
At zero degrees with a fifteen mile an hour wind, it feels like nineteen below. Exposed skin can freeze in thirty minutes.
Heads up: for you, that feels-like number is real. Cover up your skin.
